name: Monarchism
summary: Monarchism advocates monarchy, rule or headship of state by a hereditary king. The sources that name it and can be tied to it here are the counter-revolutionary writer Joseph de Maistre, who treats the Revolution as an antireligious crime crowned by regicide, and the Action Française tradition of Charles Maurras. It is mainly a doctrine about the form of the state and says little on economic or most social questions.
scope: Monarchism as the advocacy of monarchy, rule or headship of state by a monarch, independent of any one monarch. The defining sources that name it point to two strands with texts of their own: the counter-revolutionary and integral-royalist tradition (Joseph de Maistre, named a 'fanatical monarchist' by the New World Encyclopedia; Charles Maurras, who 'became an ardent monarchist' in Britannica and whose monarchism McClelland treats as his way of being a radical reactionary; Maurras's Enquête sur la monarchie, which names monarchisme and monarchistes throughout) and the scriptural, absolutist monarchism Riley's Cambridge introduction finds in Bossuet's Politics Drawn from Holy Scripture. Under today's rules only texts a defining source ties to the subject answer; Bagehot, Filmer, James VI and I, Hegel, Carlism and the Monarchist League were not tied and are left out of this draft. Silence is null, never 0.

notes: Later pass under rules 7, books pass 2026-11-25. Answers come from the tied texts: Maurras's Enquête sur la monarchie (archive.org copy; Discours préliminaire VI, IX, X, Maurras's own voice, not the respondents' replies), Bossuet's Politics (Books II and IV) and Maistre (Considérations, Essai §XXIX). Themes searched: head of state and succession, elections and democracy, parliament, decentralisation, religion and sacred rule, resistance and revolution, constitutions. Hoppe says in his own book that he is not a monarchist; Swale, Dante, Hobbes, Balmes, Farrer, Morley and Vegas Latapie are not tied to monarchism by a defining source and were not used. All other statements have no stated position in the tied sources: silence is null.
